results.title: Successors of a finite set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type and let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$. For a finite set $Z \subseteq \alpha$, the set of $r$-successors of $Z$ is the finite set $\mathrm{post}_r(Z) = \{t \in \alpha \mid r(z, t) \text{ for some } z \in Z\}$.

results.title: Elements reachable from a point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and let $a \in \alpha$. The finite set of elements reachable from $a$ is the finite set of elements reachable from the source set $\{a\}$, that is, the elements reachable from $a$ in one or more $r$-steps.

results.title: Membership in the set reachable from finitely many sources
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and let $A \subseteq \alpha$ be a finite set. An element $t \in \alpha$ lies in the finite set of elements reachable from $A$ in one or more $r$-steps (computed as a finite least fixed point) if and only if there is some $a \in A$ such that $(a, t)$ lies in the transitive closure of $r$.

results.title: Membership in the set reachable from a point
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality, let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$, and let $a \in \alpha$. An element $t \in \alpha$ lies in the finite set of elements reachable from $a$ in one or more $r$-steps (computed as a finite least fixed point) if and only if $(a, t)$ lies in the transitive closure of $r$.

results.title: Decidability of the transitive closure on a finite type
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality and let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$. Then the transitive closure of $r$ is decidable: for all $a, t \in \alpha$ it is decidable whether $t$ is reachable from $a$ in one or more $r$-steps.

results.title: Decidability of the reflexive-transitive closure on a finite type
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\alpha$ be a finite type with decidable equality and let $r$ be a decidable relation on $\alpha$. Then the reflexive-transitive closure of $r$ is decidable: for all $a, t \in \alpha$ it is decidable whether $t$ is reachable from $a$ in zero or more $r$-steps.

results.title: Cyclic sublattice of a subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be an abelian group and let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of $A$. Then $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$ when $L' \subseteq L$ and the quotient group $L/L'$ is cyclic; formally the quotient is taken by $L' \cap L$, regarded as a subgroup of $L$.

results.title: Characterization of cyclic sublattices
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of an abelian group $A$. Then $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$ if and only if $L' \subseteq L$ and the quotient group $L/(L' \cap L)$, with $L' \cap L$ regarded as a subgroup of $L$, is cyclic.

results.title: A cyclic sublattice is contained in its ambient subgroup
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of an abelian group $A$. If $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$, then $L' \subseteq L$.

results.title: The quotient by a cyclic sublattice is cyclic
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of an abelian group $A$. If $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$, then the quotient group $L/L'$ is cyclic.

results.title: Criterion for a cyclic sublattice
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $L'$ and $L$ be subgroups of an abelian group $A$. If $L' \subseteq L$ and the quotient group $L/L'$ is cyclic, then $L'$ is a cyclic sublattice of $L$.

results.title: Lucchini's coprime generation bound (Kourovka 16.53)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for every finite group $G$, all subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ of coprime orders that together generate $G$, and every natural number $d$, if each of $A$ and $B$ is generated by at most $d$ elements, then $G$ is generated by at most $d + 1$ elements.

results.title: Lucchini's coprime generation bound fails
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: There exist a finite group $G$, subgroups $A$ and $B$ of $G$ of coprime orders that together generate $G$, and a natural number $d$ such that each of $A$ and $B$ is generated by at most $d$ elements, but no set of at most $d + 1$ elements generates $G$. That is, Kourovka Problem 16.53 has a negative answer.

results.title: Constructible real numbers
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The constructible real numbers form the smallest set of real numbers that contains every rational number and is closed under addition, negation, multiplication, inverses of nonzero elements and square roots of nonnegative elements; equivalently, the smallest subfield of $\mathbb{R}$ closed under square roots.

results.title: Gauss–Wantzel number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A natural number $n$ is a Gauss–Wantzel number if $n > 0$, every prime factor of $n$ is either $2$ or a Fermat prime, and $p^2$ does not divide $n$ for every odd prime factor $p$ of $n$.

results.title: Gauss–Wantzel theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n \ge 3$, the real number $\cos(2\pi/n)$ is constructible (it lies in the smallest subfield of $\mathbb{R}$ closed under square roots) if and only if $n$ is a Gauss–Wantzel number, that is, every prime factor of $n$ is $2$ or a Fermat prime and every odd prime factor of $n$ divides $n$ only once.

results.title: Characteristic polynomial of a rank-two endomorphism
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The characteristic polynomial of an endomorphism of a free rank-two module is `X² - tr f · X + det f`, the familiar quadratic formula.

results.title: Trace and determinant are invariant under semiconjugacy
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Trace and determinant are preserved under semiconjugacy: if `e` intertwines `f` and `g`, then `g` is the conjugate of `f` by `e`, so both invariants agree.

results.title: Kernel of the dual map has the same dimension as the kernel
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The kernel of the dual map has the same finite dimension as the kernel: both are complementary to the range, by rank-nullity and the dual-annihilator dimension formula.

results.title: General linear group action on primitive vectors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Call $v \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ primitive when the greatest common divisor of its four entries is $1$. For every $X \in \mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ and every primitive $v$, the vector $Xv$ is primitive, so $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ acts on the primitive vectors of $\mathbb{Z}^4$ by $v \mapsto Xv$.

results.title: Descartes matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Descartes matrix is the $4 \times 4$ integer matrix $M$ with $M_{ii} = 1$ for every $i$ and $M_{ij} = -1$ for $i \ne j$. It is the matrix of the Descartes form: for $v = (a, b, c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ one has $v^{\mathsf T} M v = 2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2) - (a + b + c + d)^2$.

results.title: Descartes orthogonal group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M$ be the Descartes matrix. The Descartes orthogonal group is the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ consisting of the matrices $X$ with $X^{\mathsf T} M X = M$, that is, the invertible integer matrices that preserve the Descartes form $2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2) - (a + b + c + d)^2$.

results.title: Descartes orthogonal group action
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $Q$ be the set of vectors $(a, b, c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ with $(a + b + c + d)^2 = 2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2)$ and $\gcd(a, b, c, d) = 1$. For every matrix $X$ in the Descartes orthogonal group and every $v \in Q$, the vector $Xv$ lies in $Q$, so the Descartes orthogonal group acts on $Q$ by $v \mapsto Xv$.

results.title: Integral primitive Descartes quadruple
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: An integral primitive Descartes quadruple is a vector $(a, b, c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ such that $a + b + c + d > 0$, the Descartes equation $(a + b + c + d)^2 = 2(a^2 + b^2 + c^2 + d^2)$ holds, and $\gcd(a, b, c, d) = 1$.

results.title: The Apollonian generator $S_1$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: $S_1$ is the element of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ given by the $4 \times 4$ integer matrix whose first row is $(-1, 2, 2, 2)$ and whose other rows are those of the identity matrix; it is its own inverse. Acting on column vectors, it sends $(a, b, c, d)$ to $(-a + 2b + 2c + 2d, b, c, d)$.

results.title: The Apollonian generator $S_2$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: $S_2$ is the element of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ given by the $4 \times 4$ integer matrix whose second row is $(2, -1, 2, 2)$ and whose other rows are those of the identity matrix; it is its own inverse. Acting on column vectors, it sends $(a, b, c, d)$ to $(a, 2a - b + 2c + 2d, c, d)$.

results.title: The Apollonian generator $S_3$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: $S_3$ is the element of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ given by the $4 \times 4$ integer matrix whose third row is $(2, 2, -1, 2)$ and whose other rows are those of the identity matrix; it is its own inverse. Acting on column vectors, it sends $(a, b, c, d)$ to $(a, b, 2a + 2b - c + 2d, d)$.

results.title: The Apollonian generator $S_4$
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: $S_4$ is the element of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ given by the $4 \times 4$ integer matrix whose fourth row is $(2, 2, 2, -1)$ and whose other rows are those of the identity matrix; it is its own inverse. Acting on column vectors, it sends $(a, b, c, d)$ to $(a, b, c, 2a + 2b + 2c - d)$.

results.title: Apollonian group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The Apollonian group is the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ generated by the four matrices $S_1, S_2, S_3, S_4$, where $S_i$ agrees with the $4 \times 4$ identity matrix except in row $i$, which has entry $-1$ in column $i$ and entry $2$ in each of the other three columns.

results.title: The transformation group
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The transformation group is the subgroup of $\mathrm{GL}_4(\mathbb{Z})$ generated by the Apollonian group together with all $4 \times 4$ permutation matrices.

results.title: The transformation group preserves integral primitive Descartes quadruples
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $g$ in the transformation group, $g$ maps the set of integral primitive Descartes quadruples into itself: if $v \in \mathbb{Z}^4$ is an integral primitive Descartes quadruple, then so is $g v$.

results.title: Action of the transformation group on integral primitive Descartes quadruples
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Each element $g$ of the transformation group sends an integral primitive Descartes quadruple $v$ to $g v$, by matrix–vector multiplication: this is the restriction of the action of the transformation group on $\mathbb{Z}^4$ to the set of integral primitive Descartes quadruples, which is closed under the action.

results.title: Primitive Apollonian circle packing
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A primitive Apollonian circle packing is an orbit of the transformation group acting on the set of integral primitive Descartes quadruples.

results.title: Curvature set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a primitive Apollonian circle packing, viewed as an orbit of integral primitive Descartes quadruples. The curvature set of $A$ is the set of all integers that occur as an entry of some quadruple in $A$.

results.title: A packing with no square curvatures
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the primitive Apollonian circle packing generated by the integral primitive Descartes quadruple $(-3, 5, 8, 8)$. For every integer $n$, $n^2$ does not belong to the curvature set of $\mathcal{A}$.

results.title: Missing curvature set
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $A$ be a primitive Apollonian circle packing. The missing curvature set of $A$ is the set of positive integers $n$ that do not lie in the curvature set of $A$ but are congruent modulo $24$ to some element of the curvature set of $A$.

results.title: Number of missing curvatures
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a primitive Apollonian circle packing $A$ and a real number $N$, the number of missing curvatures of $A$ up to $N$ is the number of elements $n$ of the missing curvature set of $A$ with $n \le N$, regarded as a real number.

results.title: Infinitely many packings with many missing curvatures
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For a primitive Apollonian circle packing $\mathcal{A}$ and a real number $N$, let $M_{\mathcal{A}}(N)$ be the number of missing curvatures of $\mathcal{A}$ up to $N$. There are infinitely many primitive Apollonian circle packings $\mathcal{A}$ such that $\sqrt{N} = O(M_{\mathcal{A}}(N))$ as $N$ tends to infinity. In other words, for these packings the number of missing curvatures up to $N$ is $\Omega(\sqrt{N})$.

results.title: Keith sequence prefix

results.title: Keith sequence
results.caption: Definition

results.title: Keith number

results.summary: If a context-free grammar $g$ is reduced, then the binarization of $g$ is in Chomsky normal form.

results.title: Binarization preserves the language
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a context-free grammar $g$ is reduced, then the binarization of $g$ generates exactly the language of $g$.

results.title: Grammar with a fresh nullable start symbol
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given a context-free grammar $G$ with nonterminals $N$ and initial nonterminal $S$, this is the grammar with nonterminals $N \cup \{S_0\}$ for a fresh symbol $S_0$, initial nonterminal $S_0$, and the following productions: every production of $G$; the empty production $S_0 \to \varepsilon$; and $S_0 \to \alpha$ for every production $S \to \alpha$ of $G$.

results.title: Language of the grammar with a fresh nullable start symbol
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every context-free grammar $G$, the grammar obtained from $G$ by adding a fresh initial nonterminal (with an empty production and copies of the productions of the old initial nonterminal) generates exactly $L(G) \cup \{\varepsilon\}$, where $L(G)$ is the language of $G$ and $\varepsilon$ is the empty word.

results.title: The fresh start symbol occurs in no output
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every context-free grammar $g$, the fresh initial nonterminal of the fresh-start grammar of $g$ occurs in no production output of the fresh-start grammar.

results.title: A fresh start symbol is harmless when the empty word is generated
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If the empty word belongs to the language of a context-free grammar $g$, then the fresh-start grammar of $g$ generates exactly the language of $g$.

results.title: Adding a fresh start symbol preserves Chomsky normal form
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If a context-free grammar $g$ is in Chomsky normal form and no production of $g$ has empty output, then the fresh-start grammar of $g$ is in Chomsky normal form.

results.title: Chomsky normal form theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every context-free grammar $G$ there is a context-free grammar in Chomsky normal form that generates the same language as $G$.

results.title: Chomsky normal form for context-free languages
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every context-free language $L$ is generated by some context-free grammar in Chomsky normal form.

results.title: Schedule of a list of jobs
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $m$ be a natural number. An assignment $\sigma$ of a list $\sigma(i)$ of natural numbers (processing times) to each machine $i \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$ is a schedule of a list $J$ of natural numbers when the sum over all machines $i$ of the multisets of entries of $\sigma(i)$ equals the multiset of entries of $J$, that is, every number occurs in the lists $\sigma(i)$ together exactly as often as it occurs in $J$.

results.title: Makespan
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a schedule $\sigma$ that gives each of $m$ machines a list of processing times, the load of a machine is the sum of its list, and the makespan of $\sigma$ is the largest machine load ($0$ when $m = 0$).

results.title: Least-loaded machine
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $L$ assign a load $L(i) \in \mathbb{N}$ to each machine $i \in \{0, \dots, m - 1\}$. The least-loaded machine for $L$ is the smallest index $i$ at which $L(i)$ is minimal.

results.title: Longest processing time first (LPT)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given $m \ge 1$ identical machines and a list of job processing times (natural numbers), LPT sorts the jobs into nonincreasing order by merge sort and then applies Graham's list scheduling on $m$ machines to the sorted list. The cost counted is the number of comparisons made by merge sort plus the cost of list scheduling, $m$ per job.

results.title: The empty schedule
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every number $m$ of machines, the assignment of the empty list to each of the $m$ machines is a schedule of the empty list of jobs.

results.title: Every job is at most the makespan
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a schedule on $m$ machines of a list $J$ of processing times. Then every entry $x$ of $J$ is at most the makespan of $\sigma$.

results.title: Total work is at most $m$ times the makespan
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If $\sigma$ is a schedule of a list $P$ of jobs on $m$ machines, then the total processing time of $P$ is at most $m$ times the makespan of $\sigma$.

results.title: A least-loaded machine carries at most the average load
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\sigma$ be a schedule of a list $P$ of jobs on $m \ge 1$ machines, with load $\ell_i$ on machine $i$. Then $m$ times the load of a least-loaded machine is at most the total processing time $T$ of the jobs in $P$, counted with multiplicity: $m \min_i \ell_i \le T$.

results.title: Graham's bound for list scheduling
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $J$ be a list of processing times. Let $C$ be the makespan of the schedule that list scheduling on $m$ machines produces from $J$, taking the jobs in the order of $J$, and let $M$ be the makespan of any schedule of $J$ on $m$ machines. Then $mC \le (2m - 1)M$, that is, $C \le (2 - 1/m)M$.

results.title: Counting jobs when every machine is heavily loaded
results.caption: Theorem

If every job in $P$ is at least $p$ and every machine has load (the sum of its jobs) greater than $d$, then $2m \le n + k$, where $n$ is the number of jobs in $P$ and $k$ is the number of jobs $x$ in $P$ with $p \le x$ and $x > d$, both counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Graham's bound for LPT scheduling
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $m \ge 1$ and let $J$ be a list of natural numbers (job processing times). Let $C$ be the makespan of the schedule of $J$ on $m$ machines produced by the LPT algorithm, and let $M$ be the makespan of any schedule $\tau$ of $J$ on $m$ machines. results.title: List scheduling schedules every job
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $m \ge 1$ and every list $J$ of processing times, the assignment that list scheduling on $m$ machines produces from $J$ is a schedule of $J$.

results.title: Running time of list scheduling
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For $m \ge 1$ and every list of $n$ jobs, list scheduling on $m$ machines has cost exactly $nm$, in the cost model that charges $m$ for each job placed (one unit per machine load inspected).

results.title: Running time of LPT
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: On $m \ge 1$ machines and a list of $n$ jobs, LPT costs at most $n \lceil \log_2 n \rceil + nm$, counting merge-sort comparisons and machine load inspections.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a real $\delta$, two tagged points $a$ and $b$ are same-side far apart when, if $a$ and $b$ carry the same side, the squared distance between their points is at least $\delta$.

results.title: Strip points
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Given reals $\delta$ and $x_{\mathrm{mid}}$, a tagged point $((x, y), s)$ lies in the strip when $(x - x_{\mathrm{mid}})^2 < \delta$, and moreover $x \le x_{\mathrm{mid}}$ if its side $s$ is left ($s$ false) and $x_{\mathrm{mid}} \le x$ if its side $s$ is right ($s$ true).

results.summary: Let $\delta$ be a real, $q = (q_1, q_2)$ a point of $\mathbb{R}^2$ and $L$ a list of points of $\mathbb{R}^2$. results.title: Two ones combine into a two in the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Index the Fibonacci numbers as $F_1 = 1$, $F_2 = 2$, $F_{i+1} = F_i + F_{i-1}$. Passing from the state consisting of two copies of $F_1$ to the state consisting of one copy of $F_2$ is a move of the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game.

results.title: No move from the empty state
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: No move takes the empty state (no copies of any $F_i$) to any state.

results.title: Complete Accelerated Zeckendorf Games
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A sequence of states $g_0, g_1, \dots$ is a complete Accelerated Zeckendorf Game on $n$ with $L$ moves if $g_0$ consists of $n$ copies of $F_1$, for every $j < L$ some move takes $g_j$ to $g_{j+1}$, and no move is possible from $g_L$. The states after $g_L$ play no role.

results.title: The complete game on $0$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The sequence whose states are all the empty state is a complete Accelerated Zeckendorf Game on $0$ with $0$ moves.

results.title: Losing states of the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: The losing and the winning states of the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game are defined by simultaneous induction: a state is losing when every move from it leads to a winning state, and a state is winning when some move from it leads to a losing state. In particular every state from which no move is possible is losing.

results.title: Winning states of the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game
results.caption: Inductive
results.summary: A state $s$ is winning (the player to move has a winning strategy) if some move takes $s$ to a losing state. Winning and losing states are defined by simultaneous induction: a state is losing if every move from it reaches a winning state.

results.title: Characterization of winning states
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A state $s$ is winning if and only if some move takes $s$ to a losing state.

results.title: Terminal states are losing in the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Every state of the Accelerated Zeckendorf Game from which no move is possible is a losing state.

results.title: The first player wins the game on $2$
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The state consisting of two copies of $F_1$ is winning.
